On the forms of this verb it has been explained in detail in Thes. vol. 8 p. 714-716 and by Veitch p. 590-595, third edition. Aeschylus often used the present φέρω [I bear] and φέρομαι [I bear for myself]: of other tenses there are very few examples, of the aorist infinitive ἐνεγκεῖν [to have brought], of the future middle οἴσεσθαι [to be about to bring for oneself] Prom. 638.
